2. The short facts for disposal of plaintiffs case is that, the suit land originally belonged to Emdadul Hossain and Abdul Aziz Contractor and accordingly the R.S. Khatian was recorded rightly in the name of Enidadul Hossain and by a mere mistake in the name of Moshiuddowla, son of Abdul Aziz. Abdul  Aziz Sonazan and Latifa Khatun while in possession of the suit land sold out the same by a registered kabala No. 3159 dated 16.08.35 A.D to Sultan Ahmed, son of Abdul Gafur R.S. recorded Emdad Hossain died leaving behind his paternal aunt Srimati Sonajan four sisters namely Srimati Rabeya Khatun, Srimati Ambia Khatun, Srimati Zahera Khatun alias Bechau and Srimati Nazma. Khatun and his wife Srimati Sofeya Khatun as his heirs. The said heirs transferred 21 satak or 10'/z ganda land to Sultan Ahmed minor son of. Abdul Gafur by a registered kabala No. 3231 dated 28.08.35 A.D. Abdul Garur purchased the lands of above kabalas in the benami of his minor son Sultan Ahmed. The said Sultan Ahmed being on unmarried person died during the life time of his father, Abdul Garur who became the owner and possessor of suit land left by his son. Besides the suit land Abdul Garur was the owner of six kani fourteen gandas of land. Thus he became owner of lands measuring I0(ten) kanis Abdul Gafur transferred the suit land by a registered wasiyat nama no. 6 dated 05.04.1958 A.D. to his only daughter Azab Khatun and thereafter Azab Khatun was in possession of the suit land and accordingly P.S. Khatian No. 1281 was prepared in her name. The said Azab Khatun died leaving behind the plaintiffs and proforma defendants nos. 9 and 10 on 8.10.1991 A.D. Plaintiff no. 1 Eusuf All went to the Tashil office for paying rent of the suit land but the Tashilder received rent for 7 (seven) gonads and 1 (one) Kara of land and refused to accept rent for the rest suit land of 13(thirteen) gandas and 3(three) karas on the ground that B.S. Khatian no. 2223 comprising suit land (thirteen ganda three kara) and other lands have been prepared in the name of Mahmud Mia, father of the defendant. After that the plaintiff on 8.10.1992 A.D. obtained certified copy of the B.S. Khatian no. 2223 and from that he fully came to know that the B.S. Khatian of suit land mentioned in schedule 1(ka) has been prepared and recorded in the name of Mahmud Mia, father of defendant Nos. 1-8. Moreover on 16.12.98 A.D. predecessor of the defendants threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs claimed their title over suit land. Due to 

 wrong B.S. khatian of the suit land and threat of dispossession by the defendants predecessor the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in the suit land has been clouded. For removing the said cloudness the plaintiffs have been constrained to file the present suit. 

 3. On the other hand, the defendant Nos. and 3 contested the suit by filing written statement separately contending, inter alia, that Abdul Hamid Sowdagar being decree holder of execution case no. 234/265 in the 2nd Munsif Court purchased the suit land in auction and has been in possession of the same by a certificate of sale. The said Abdul Humid Sowdagar while in possession of the suit land and other land transferred the same by a registered kabala no. 3769 to Korban Ali Sowdagar, the grandfather of the defendants and delivered possession to him. After the death of Korban Ali Sowdagar his only son Mohammad Mia became owner of the suit land and other lands left by his father. Thereafter the said Mohammed Mia Sowdagar has been in possession of the suit land. After that Mohammed Mia Sowdagar gave permission to plaintiffs mother Azab Khatun to live in the land of P.S. Plot no. 1832. Then Mohammed Mia Sowdagar has erected pucca boundary wall around land of P.S. plot no. 1830, 1831 and 1833 and constructed semi pucca house there and let the houses to tenants for temporary period. The land of said P.S. Plot Nos. 1830, 1831 and 1833 has been rightly recorded in the name of Mohammed Mia in P.S. Khatian. The land of P.S. Plot no. 1832 was wrongly recorded in P.S. Khatian in the name of plaintiffs mother, Azab Khatun who is merely a permissive possessor of the suit land. However after the death of Mohammed Mia Sowdagar his heirs including. Plaintiff Nos. I and 3 became owners of the suit land. Then plaintiffs Nos. I and 3 became owner of suit property of P.S. Plot Nos. 1830, 1831, 1832 by partition and opened B.S. Mutation Khatian Nos. 2929 and 2985 in their name by filing mutation case no. 1005/92-93 and 3865/93-94, since then the defendants got connection of electricity and water supply and they had their name in holding of City Corporation. The defendants Nos. I and 3 further state that they obtained adverse possession-in the suit land and that the plaintiffs like- their mother are mere permissive possession of the suit land. The plaintiffs and their predecessor have no right, title, interest and possession over the suit land and for that the defendants have prayed for dismissal of the present suit. 

 8. Mr. Md. Abdul Quayum the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant submits (hat the learned trial Court below committed error of law and fact and decreed the suit and the learned trial Court did not appreciate that the suit was barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The learned Advocate appearing for the appellants further submits that the learned trial Court did not apply its judicial mind and decreed the suit upon conjecture and surmise and the learned court below did not appreciate that the plaintiff could not prove possession and yet decreed the suit. The learned Advocate appearing for the appellant also submits that the learned trial Court wrongly shifted the onus upon the defendants appellants thus decreed the suit and the learned trial Court wrongly did not make the kabala of the defendant into evidence. The Court below ought to have found that the plaintiff failed to prove their case'. The learned Advocate appearing for the appellants then submits that the finding of the learned trial Court about oral gift by the plaintiff and admission of the interest of the mother of the plaintiff is not correct and erroneous and the trial Court relied upon evidence beyond pleadings and did not consider reply to the interrogation as to existence of boundary wall, electric and gas connection, The learned Advocate appearing for the appellant further submits that the trial court admitted into evidence certified copies filed by the plaintiff but did not mark as exhibits into evidence of the document dated 15.10.1935. Thus he committed error of law occasioning failure of justice and the finding of the trial Court about the R.S. Khatian is mistaken and liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate appearing for the appellant again submits that the learned trial Court below did not appreciate that Azufa Khatun was given permissive possession to stay which is not disputed land and the learned trial Court did not consider that the plaintiff did not file any paper relating to payment of rent, holding tax receipt and" electricity bill and on the contrary the appellants filed those documents which has been marked in evidence as exhibits Kha, Ga,Ga(1) Gha, Gha(I) rent receipt Uma, electricity bill Chha and Chha(1) and the finding that the electric connection in the name of the brother of the plaintiff is wrong and erroneous. The learned Advocate appearing for appellant lastly submits that the finding of the trial Court misconstructed the exhibit-8, the learned trial court ought to have dismissed the suit on finding of earlier suit which failed and the learned trial Court did not apply his judicial mind to the deposition as to possession and decreed the suit most illegally upon misconception of law and did not advert to the statement of the P.W. I that the B.S. Khatian is correct and the learned trial Court did not advert to the material evidence and decreed the suit upon conjecture and surmise and as such the erroneous finding of the trial Court is not at all sustainable in law and the same deserves our interference under the appellate jurisdiction of this Hon’ble Court.
